Power consumption decreased approximately 58%, which directly lowers the data center’s cooling load by 26 tons of refrigeration, equivalent to nearly 316,000 BTU/hr. This reduction translates into lower annual operating costs for both electrical and mechanical cooling systems. At the same time, compute core capacity increased by 21%, enabling higher throughput and more efficient use of data center resources within the same rack footprint. This transition also simplified system administration by eliminating the complexity of maintaining multiple aging clusters, reducing maintenance overhead, and standardizing the software and user environment. The resulting configuration positions FFESD and ITSD HPC to meet evolving research demands, reduce operational costs, and align with institutional Operational Excellence performance pillars, while achieving energy efficiency and sustainability goals. 7 CREDITS AND CONTRIBUTORS The successful launch of the FFESD flagship cluster, Helios, and the excision of the Legacy Clusters required a tremendous collective effort by many individuals.
